issue.title: Use soft-deletes to maintain document history

labels.name: :Distributed/Engine
labels.description: Anything around managing Lucene and the Translog in an open shard.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
With the introduction of [soft-delete]((https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LUCENE-8200)) in Lucene, a history of a document can be maintained. This meta issue tracks work on migrating from hard-deletes to soft-deletes.

Cut over
--------
- [x] Replace hard-updates by soft-updates (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/29458)
- [x] Replace hard-deletes by soft-deletes (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/29549)
- [x] Index no-op (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/30226) 
- [x] Index stale operations (i.e. out of order) on replicas (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/29679)

Retention and source
--------------------
- [x] Use SoftDeletesRetentionMergePolicy to maintain only the recent history (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/30335)
- [x] Special merge strategy when `_source` is disabled (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/31106)
- ~~Do not keep delete tombstones in version map. Delete tombstones can be queried from Lucene~~ (to be done in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/31637)

Translog
--------
- [x] Add API allows querying operations given a range of seq# (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/30120)
- ~~Use `maxTimestamp` from engine for `autoGeneratedIdTimestamp`~~ (migrated to #30086)
- [x] Replace translog by Lucene history in peer-recovery (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/30522)
- [x] Replace translog by Lucene history in primary-replica resync (#33178)
- [x] Only sends operations after the local checkpoint in peer-recovery (#33190)

TBD
-------
- ~~Avoid having multiple docs for the same stale operation. We currently defer the dedup until the search time but we might revisit this decision to do it at the index time~~(to be done in #31637). 

Misc
-------
- [x] Store the reason of noop in its document tombstone (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/30570)
- [x] Use exact numDocs in synced-flush (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/30228)
- [x] Randomize soft-deletes settings (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/31585)
- [x] Do not expose hard-deleted documents (#32333)

body: I see a solution that brings a deleted doc to live iff it was soft-deleted. However, this approach may be fragile for stale documents (soft-deleted before indexing) because it relies on the order of processing fields. If the soft-deletes field of a doc is processed then that doc is aborted, we can't exclude that document from liveDocs. Another option is to expose hard liveDocs in Lucene.
I think we can expose the actual hard deletes on a SegmentReader level. that is the best solution IMO.

issue.title: Do not expose hard-deleted docs in Lucene history

labels.name: :Distributed/Engine
labels.description: Anything around managing Lucene and the Translog in an open shard.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Today when reading operation history in Lucene, we read all documents.
However, if indexing a document is aborted, IndexWriter will hard-delete
it; we, therefore, need to exclude that document from Lucene history.

This commit makes sure that we exclude aborted documents by using the
hard liveDocs of a SegmentReader if there are deletes.

Closes #32269
